> **Status: default selected on corpus A; N2 not yet confirmed.**
> - Run `2026-10-03T09-10-49Z` on **corpus A** (13.2A, the user's own voice, microphone and room; 40 utterances), same matrix as the 2026-09-17 corpus-B run. Conditions: AC, `performance` platform profile, VS Code open, package 74 °C at start, 82–86 °C for most of the run (99 °C only during the first configuration).
> - Default: `small-q8_0`, `threads = 4`, `audio_ctx = 1000` — WER 7.4 %, p90 text_ready 3.73 → **3.67 s**, peak RSS 467 MB. It is again the only production configuration with p90 ≤ 5 s, so the corpus-B selection (2026-09-17) stands. N2 is confirmed only by the v0.1 `total` measurement with injection (13 §13.5).
> - WER on corpus A is about a third of corpus B (7.4 % vs 24.1 % for the default); latency is within 2 % of the corpus-B run.
> - `audio_ctx = 1000` costs nothing on the whole corpus for `small-q8_0` (7.5 → 7.4 %) and saves ~35 % latency; for `small-q5_1` it costs 0.9 pp (7.8 → 8.7 %). Both stay inside the 1 pp limit of 13 §13.5.
> - Runner-up `small-q5_1` @1000 is worse here (8.7 %) and again just above N2 (p90 5.07 s); beam 5 gains 0.5–1.1 pp but costs 1.2–1.5 s p90.
> - **Short utterances are the weak spot:** `small-q8_0` @1000 has 18.1 % WER on the `short` group (12 sentences of 3–5 words, so one wrong word ≈ 2 pp) vs 7.1 % on `medium`. This is the typical PTT case — revisit in v0.1/v0.2 (VAD trimming, prompt).
> - `difficult` (4 sentences only): `audio_ctx = 1000` scores 18.0 % vs 14.8 % with the full window — a signal, not a conclusion, at this sample size.
> - `medium-q5_0` halves the error (3.8 % vs 7.6 % on the medium group) but needs p50 15.0 s even @1000 — eliminated on this CPU.
> - Not measured on corpus A: `small` (f16), 8 threads, the `long/` continuous recording (soak test, v0.2), `total` with injection (v0.1).

## History — interim public corpus B (2026-09-17)

Run `2026-09-17T16-28-19Z` on `/home/leto/stt-corpus-public` (13.2B: FLEURS + Wolne Lektury audiobook, other speakers, studio-like audio, no `short` group). It produced the provisional default that corpus A later confirmed. Notes from that run:

> - Run on the interim public corpus (13.2B), not corpus A. Rerun on corpus A before fixing the defaults for good.
> - Provisional default: `small-q8_0`, `threads = 4`, `audio_ctx = 1000` (WER 24.1 %, p90 text_ready 3.73 s, peak RSS 442 MB). Approved by the user on 2026-09-17 under the 13 §13.5 rule with N2 = 5 s.
> - Runner-up `small-q5_1` @1000 is 1.8 pp better (WER 22.3 %) but measured p90 5.07 s and 5.10 s in two runs, i.e. above N2 before injection is even counted; the user chose the configuration that satisfies the rule.
> - Repeatability check (run `2026-09-17T18-48-42Z-rerun-ctx1000`, both `@1000` configurations, whole corpus): p50/p90 within 0.6–4.7 % of this run and all 84 transcripts per configuration identical character for character. On a cool, idle machine on AC the spread is far below the ±20 % seen in the first session.
> - `audio_ctx = 1000` costs at most 0.8 pp WER (`small-q8_0` 23.3 → 24.1 %) and saves 30–37 % latency; for `small-q5_1` it slightly improved WER (22.7 → 22.3 %). Both stay inside the 1 pp limit of 13 §13.5.
> - Request history matters (06 §6.7): `small-q8_0` @1000 scores 23.8 % WER on the medium group alone (stage 1) and 24.2 % when the same files are interleaved with longer full-window recordings (stage 2). Stage 2 is the production-like order.
> - `medium-q5_0` is eliminated even with `audio_ctx = 1000` (p50 15.1 s), and `large-v3-turbo-q5_0` is far slower still (whisper-bench encoder 39.3 s vs 20.6 s for medium).
> - `small` (f16), measured separately on 2026-09-18 (run `2026-09-18T18-53-52Z-small-f16`, same runner and order): @1000 WER 23.7 %, p90 4.56 s, peak RSS 658 MB; full window WER 22.7 %, p90 6.67 s. @1000 meets N2 but is within 1 pp of the default (−0.4 pp), so the 13 §13.5 tie-break (lower peak RAM) keeps `small-q8_0` (442 MB) as the default. Cross-run comparison: WER is deterministic, latency on this machine repeats within a few %.
> - Not measured here: 8 threads (≤ 3 % gain in the first run), the `short` group (missing from the public corpus), and `total` with injection (v0.1, 13 §13.5).
